pr_body:
* Simplified code a lot, bias based on normalized cascade size.
* Lets scale cascades, max distance, etc. without creating acne.
* Fixed normal biasing in directional shadows.

I removed normal biasing in both omni and spot shadows, since the technique can't be easily implemented there.
Will need to be replaced by something else.

*Bugsquad edit: This closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/45115.*

issue_context.title: Vulkan: Directional light shadow rendering is broken on some splits after culling changes
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:** Git https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/8e514bbf6ab3d2cff4daeb64e842bd8846c07046

**OS/device including version:** Fedora 33, GeForce GTX 1080

**Issue description:** Directional light shadow rendering is broken on some splits after the recent culling changes. Also, the bias values look much larger than before even though the property defaults didn't change. You need to decrease them by a 10× factor to get the previous look again.

As you can notice on the video below, the fade is never visible even though the DirectionalLight's **Fade Start** property is at the default value (0.8).

*I bisected the regression to 548524152ebb96a176b57266514003ad2e348f6e.*

**Steps to reproduce:**

- Add a DirectionalLight node.
- Enable shadows on the DirectionalLight.
- Play around with the DirectionalLight shadow's **Max Distance** property if you want to better see the effect.

**Minimal reproduction project:** [test_directional_light_cull.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/5798817/test_directional_light_cull.zip)

### Current broken status

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/180032/104247440-1de7e200-5468-11eb-9aa8-0ff1e048290a.mp4

### Expected appearance

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/180032/104251580-55f32300-5470-11eb-89fa-23dde33aeab7.mp4
